mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, I want you to remember—healing from abuse isn’t a straight line, and there’s no timer on your journey. It’s about finding your way back to yourself, learning to trust again, and discovering meaning that goes deeper than the pain you’ve experienced. Sure, there’ll be tough days—triggers, setbacks, and moments when you question if you’re making any progress. But you’ll also find small wins, new connections, and a hope that keeps growing, little by little. So, what does this all mean for you? Healing doesn’t always move in a straight line—sometimes you’ll stumble, and that’s completely normal. Those setbacks? They don’t erase how far you’ve come. Taking care of yourself isn’t selfish—it’s essential. Every act of self-care helps rebuild your sense of worth. When triggers show up, see them as part of the process. Every time you manage them, you’re building real resilience. Reclaiming your identity means making choices for yourself—not for anyone else. And yes, healthy relationships can be yours, but it’ll take patience, trust, and a few new boundaries along the way. If you’re walking this path right now, hear this: you’re not alone, and you’re absolutely not broken. The scars you carry? They don’t make you weak. They’re proof that you’ve survived, and you’re still moving forward. Every single step you take—no matter how small—is a sign of your strength and your ability to grow. So give yourself permission to go at your own pace. Reach out for support when you need it. And don’t forget to celebrate those moments of joy and connection, no matter how brief. Healing is possible. Your story isn’t finished yet. The future? It’s yours to shape, one day at a time.
